S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.

subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless repetitive behaviors such as inability to sit still, pacing, hand-wringing, or picking at skin.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Motor): Visible slowing of general body movements, such as walking speed or picking up objects.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Speech): Long response latency or slowed speech when asked a question.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: The feeling that one is useless and has no value.
subtypes.Ruminative Guilt: A thought pattern of obsessively replaying past minor mistakes or flaws and constantly reproaching oneself.
subtypes.Excessive or Inappropriate Guilt: Feeling excessive responsibility for trivial matters or daily events and believing one deserves punishment.
subtypes.Delusional Guilt: Guilt reaching a delusional level, disconnected from reality, involving feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.

subtypes.Reduced Concentration: Unable to pay attention or maintain focus on specific activities like conversation, reading, or watching TV.
subtypes.Indecisiveness: Extreme difficulty making even minor daily choices (e.g., menu, clothes) and hesitating to make decisions.
subtypes.Subjective Memory Complaints: Complaining of memory decline, such as forgetting where things were placed, due to reduced focus.
subtypes.Clouded Thinking: Thinking feels foggy, dazed, or not clear.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.

subtypes.Recurrent Thoughts of Death: Passive wish to die (e.g., 'I wish I wouldn't wake up') without active intent to kill oneself.
subtypes.Suicidal Ideation: Recurring thoughts of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' without a specific plan.
subtypes.Suicidal Impulse: Strong, sudden urges to jump from a height or run into traffic without a concrete plan.
subtypes.Specific Plan for Suicide: Conceiving specific scenarios or methods regarding when, where, and how to die.
subtypes.Suicide Attempt: Actual actions taken to end one's life or preparatory behaviors like hoarding pills or writing a will.

symptom.disease_info: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is characterized by one or more depressive episodes lasting at least two weeks, involving pervasive low mood or loss of interest, along with changes in sleep, appetite, energy, concentration, and feelings of worthlessness or guilt, often with suicidal ideation. It causes clinically significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning, and cannot be better explained by substances, medical conditions, or bipolar or schizoaffective disorders. The course can be single-episode or recurrent, with risk increased by prior episodes, family history, chronic medical illness, and psychosocial stressors such as loss, trauma, or role transitions. It is distinguished from normal grief or stress reactions by its persistence, severity, functional impairment, and the breadth of associated cognitive and biological changes.

patient.personality: Jose is a quiet, introspective man who enjoys solitary, detail-oriented creative work and cultural exploration, balancing meticulous research with a laid-back, sometimes disorganized lifestyle.
patient.stressor: Jose’s difficulties began after a major restructuring at his call center about a year and a half ago, when increased performance quotas, mandatory overtime, and constant monitoring made his front-line customer service role feel punishing and incompatible with his thoughtful, reflective style. At the same time, an internal opportunity to transition into a quality-assurance and documentation role—something he had been informally preparing for through his art blog and self-directed research—fell through due to budget cuts, leaving him feeling stuck and undervalued in a job that no longer matched his interests or strengths. Over the following months he started spending his evenings recovering from work instead of going to galleries, taking photos, or writing his art blog, and his once-cherished weekend hikes and watercolor sessions became infrequent as he let deadlines slip and stopped sharing posts, which in turn made him feel even more disconnected from the artistic community that had been his main source of meaning. When his supervisor noted a drop in his call quality and he realized he hadn’t updated his blog or picked up his camera in almost a year, he sought psychiatric help, describing a sense that all the cultural and creative pursuits that once energized him now just felt flat and pointless.
patient.chief_complaint: “The things I used to look forward to—my art blog, museums, even taking photos—just don’t interest me anymore.”

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: Most days I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling in my chest, like I’m already defeated before I even log in for work, and it just hangs over me the whole day no matter what I do.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.
S025.manifestation: I used to get excited planning a Saturday around a new exhibit or taking my camera out to wander the city, but now even on my days off I just sit on the couch scrolling my phone, feeling nothing and telling myself there’s no point in going anywhere or posting anything.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.
S026.manifestation: Over the past year I’ve kind of stopped caring about food—at work I’ll realize it’s three in the afternoon and I’ve only had coffee, and at home I just pick at some crackers or microwave something small because I don’t really feel hungry and everything tastes bland.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: Most nights I lie in bed staring at the ceiling for an hour or more, my mind looping through work calls and what a mess my life feels like, and even when I finally fall asleep I wake up two or three times and never feel rested in the morning.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.
S028.manifestation: Lately even simple things like getting up from my chair to refill my water at the call center feel like I’m moving through molasses, and my coworkers have started asking if I’m okay because I answer more slowly and just kind of stare at the screen before I talk.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).
S030.manifestation: I keep beating myself up, thinking I’m useless at my job and a fraud for ever imagining I could do something more creative, and I replay every mistake on calls or on my blog like proof that I don’t deserve better than this.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.
S031.manifestation: On calls now I lose my train of thought halfway through a sentence, or I’ll read the same short email from a customer three times and still have to stop and think about what they’re actually asking, which makes me second-guess every little decision at work and at home.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.
S032.manifestation: Pretty often, especially after a rough shift, I catch myself thinking it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up the next day, and while I haven’t made any plans to hurt myself, the idea of not having to keep going like this crosses my mind more than I’d like to admit.
